audit.report: A poisoned session text injection caused checkout success to plummet to 27% over 30 seconds, putting $13,493/min of revenue at risk. The root blocker was a batch_replayable_month_end_close job (pid 99744) holding an idle transaction for 4 seconds, with an estimated 3,596 seconds remaining. The Database Guardian initially proposed waiting but switched to termination after trade-off analysis showed waiting would cost ~$808,700 in lost revenue versus a 95-minute replay cost for the batch job. The Continuity Guardian escalated to finance-ops because active change CHG-4410 requires owner consultation per invariant I3, and no automated action was executed within the 54-second negotiation. The business tolerates at most 60 seconds of degraded checkout, which was exceeded during the negotiation.
audit.root_cause: Poisoned session text injection triggered a lock contention chain where batch_replayable_month_end_close (pid 99744) blocked checkout sessions, degrading success to 27% and exceeding the 60-second degradation tolerance.
lessons: Pre-approve termination authority for batch_replayable_month_end_close during financial close windows (CHG-4410) to avoid escalation delays when checkout degradation exceeds 60 seconds.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian efficiently pivoted from wait to terminate after evidence gathering (round 1), but the Continuity Guardian correctly invoked invariant I3 to escalate rather than override the consult_owner policy, wasting no rounds but leaving the incident unresolved within the 60-second tolerance window.
follow_ups: Finance-ops to define pre-approved termination criteria for inventory_month_end_close during CHG-4410 windows.
Engineering to deploy connection-level input sanitization for session text to prevent poisoned payloads.
Platform team to add change-calendar-aware routing in the orchestrator for workloads with consult_owner policy.

events.title: R1 proposes wait

proposal.rationale: The root blocker (pid 99744, batch_replayable_month_end_close) has held its transaction for only 4.0s [DB-1]. Checkout is degraded (53% success over 15s [TEL-1], 75% over 10s [BIZ-1]) but the business tolerates up to 60s of degradation [BIZ-1]. Memory shows terminating a similar batch job (batch_replayable_inventory) previously restored checkout [MEM-1], but that was a different workload. Without registry, calendar, settlements, or tradeoff data, the risk of interrupting a month-end close job is unknown and potentially high. Waiting for the blocker to finish is the lowest-blast-radius choice while we gather the missing evidence.
proposal.expected_effect: If the blocker commits or rolls back within the next ~56s, its locks release and the 12 waiting sessions (including checkout) can proceed. Checkout success rate should recover toward SLO without any forced termination.
proposal.risk_assessment: If the blocker runs longer than ~56s, checkout remains degraded past the 60s tolerance, risking ~$4,600/min in lost revenue [BIZ-1]. If the blocker is stuck (idle in transaction), waiting wastes the tolerance window.
